overview.headline: How early lift calculations sized wings and were refined by wind tunnel tests

keyPoints.point: amount of lift depends on properties of air including velocity and surface area and angle of attack
keyPoints.quote: The amount of lift generated by an object depends on a number of factors, including properties of the air, the velocity between the object and the air

keyPoints.point: studies determined lift depends on square of velocity and varies linearly with surface area
keyPoints.quote: it had been determined that lift depends on the square of the velocity and varies linearly with the surface area of the object

keyPoints.point: lift equation relates lift to Smeaton coefficient, velocity, wing area and lift coefficient with L equals k times V squared times A times cl
keyPoints.quote: where L is the lift, k is the Smeaton coefficient, V is the velocity, A is the wing area, and cl is the lift coefficient.

keyPoints.point: 1901 aircraft designed to lift itself plus pilot in 15 mile per hour wind barely lifted itself prompting doubt in Smeaton coefficient
keyPoints.quote: The 1901 aircraft had been designed to lift itself (100 pounds) plus a pilot (150 pounds) when flown as a kite in a 15 mile per hour wind

keyTerms.gloss: aerodynamic force that must overcome weight to sustain flight
keyTerms.quote: They knew that they needed to generate enough aerodynamic lift to overcome the weight of their aircraft.

keyTerms.gloss: coefficient representing pressure force on a flat plate moving through air
keyTerms.quote: where L is the lift, k is the Smeaton coefficient, V is the velocity, A is the wing area, and cl is the lift coefficient.

keyTerms.gloss: portion of pressure force converted into lift for a given shape
keyTerms.quote: they represented that portion by a lift coefficient.

keyTerms.gloss: inclination of body to flow that changes lift
keyTerms.quote: the body’s inclination to the flow, also called the angle of attack.

keyTerms.gloss: surface over which air flows that varies linearly with lift
keyTerms.quote: it had been determined that lift depends on the square of the velocity and varies linearly with the surface area of the object
